• WA PRINGTON POLICE COURT. MONDAY.—Befere the Mayor (Alderman Pickmere), and Major Cartwright. "A TERROR To THE PLAczY—Peter Massey, otherwise Swift, a young man, was charged with committing damage to certain glasses and jugs, the property of Mrs. Kate Jenks, to the amount of 45., on the 29th October. Isaac Smith was charged' with assaulting Mrs. Jenks.—The prosecutrix is a widow and keeps the Railway Tavern,below Bank Quay Bridge. Prisoner went into her house on the date in ques- tion between three and four o'clock in the afternoon, and had several glasses of beer. After some time Massey com- menced wrestling in the middle of the room and knocked against an old man whose son remonstrated with Massey stating he did not like 'to see his father knocked about. Smith "came out" with very bad language, knocked a glass over and broke it. She ordered the prisoners out but they refused to go. Smith "began of" one of the men in the house and Massey took his part, the young man being scandalously used. Massey then commenced to throw abottt the jugs and glasses which went against the wall " like cannon balls." The other prisoner got hold of rbe landlady, "wrestled with her like a man," and tried to get her down in the lobby and to hit her.—The Mayor said this was a most disgraceful and cowardly action.—Major Cartwright said he did not think there could be two worse men. They Iwere a terror to the place.—Prisoners were each committed for two months' hard labour.

FRODSHAM. SALE OF WORK.—A sale of useful and fancy. goods was held in the Town Hall, Frodsham, on Tuesday, m aid of the funds for a house which is in course of erection for the minister of the United Methodibt Free Church. The pro- ceedings commenced with singing and prayer, and an appro- priate address was given by Geo. Slater, Esq., of Northwich. There was a good demand, for the various articles, and the usual exhibition of arts and sciences (!) and other attrac- tions helped to increase the proceeds. SERVICE or SONO.—A service of sacred song, entitled "The Creation," was given in the Town Hall, Frodsham, on Thursday, by the choir of St. John's Presbyterian Chapel, Runcorn, the connective readings being rendered by the Revs. P. Schofield, R. P. Borwick, and E. Williams. Mr. W. B. Gibson presided. The choir acquitted themselves very creditably, the various hymns, ch., being taken up promptly, and were given with feeling and crispness, which gave evidence of their careful training. Mr. J.Cloug h was the accompanist and Mr. J. E. Warbur ton the conductor. A collection was made at the close of the service.

WElNEamon—Before Alderman Davies and Alderman Challdley. ALLEGED FRAUDULENT ENLISTMENT: STRANGE CASE. —Jan Sutherland was charged with fraudulent enlistment on the 27th October. Prisoner had been previously enlisted at Lichfield and rejected.—Sergeant Cambridge said he was instructed to press the case against the prisoner as these cases were becoming very common and theygave the mili- tary authorities a great deal of trouble. Prisoner stated one of the recruiting sergeants asked him to enlist and he showed him his paper of rejection, but tlitisergeant advised him to tear it up and go' for enlistment. e went with the sergeant but did not tear up the paper which he gave to another sergeant afterwards, and he was brought up on the present charge.—The Bench remanded the prisoner to allow enqui- ries to be made regarding the statement of the prisoner, who had made a most serious charge against the miliiary.

HALTON MIIIVAL IMPROVKIKENT SOCIETY, —On Mon- day evening Mr. S. Barrow read a paper on "Farmers' grievances," in the Wesleyan school-room. The Rev. J. Bateman, president, occupied the chair. The paper was discussed by Messrs. T. Miller, A. E. Davies, G. Pennington, B. Haddock, J. Bagnley. There was a good attendance of members.

A letter was also read from Mr. G. Fereday Smith, chief agent to the Bridgewater trustees, forwarding the copy of a communication he 'had addressed to the Local Government Board on the subject of the new building bye-laws. The copy letter stated that it had come to the knowledge of the Bridgewater and the Earl of Ellesmere trustees that the Commissioners were applying for confirmation of the new bye-laws, by section 54 of which it was prescribed that "no new street intended for a carriage road shall be laid out, or formed, of less width than 36 feet," and that the concluding words of section one prohibited any house being hereafter built within 18 feet of the centre of any carriage road, with- out the written consent of the Commissioners," and further that the latter part of section three prescribed that "in laying out new streets when back streets, or passages, were required, such passages should be provided not less than 9 feet in width." The Bridge- water and Ellesmere trustees respectively were owners of extensive estates within the district of the Commissioners to which the proposed bye-laws would apply, and on behalf of such trustees, Mr. Smith wished to draw the attention of the Local Government Board to the fact that the trustees had laid out portions of their building land estates, and in doing se they had, in accordance with the existing bye-laws of the Commissioners, provided for pas- sages of about 6ft. in width, which was much more than the width those gentlemen had hitherto required. The trustees were perfectly willing that in the future laying out of their building land no street should be of less width than 361 t. ; and no passage of less width than 91t. ; but in the cases above alluded to such width of 36ft. and 9ft. respectively could not be given without serious detriment and pecuniary loss, especially in those cases where the streets were par- tially built up to. Under such circumstances, Mr. Smith asked that before confirming the proposed new bye-laws the Local Government Board would kindly allow time for the said trustees to endeavour to arrange satisfactorily with the Commissioners regarding the streets and passages already laid out. A letter dated the sth inst., and addressed to the Sur- veyor, was also read by the Clerk, from Mr. James Kirk- ham, on behalf of the Master Builders' Association, of Run- corn. It stated that, if not too late, the association desired to call the attention of the Surveyor to the 33rd clause in the proposed revision of the Building Bye-laws. If the chimney " jambs " or " breast " were not allowed more than the 9in, projection from the face of the wall there could only be a 44,in. flue, which they conaidered scarcely of any use. They wished to know if such was the meaning of the bye-law referred to. They also wished to refer to the 9ft. passage spoken of in clause 3, which the association con- sidered objectionable, except such 9ft. passage were adopted by the Commissioners, and the property owners paved them. If left unadopted they would become a place for refuse and filth and a nuisance to a neighbourhood by being a place for the roughs of the iown to play their games. There was evidence of this, and complaints about it at NVidnes. The association also thought that section 55 should be a little modified. They were of opinion that in every case 14 days' notice previous to the Board's monthly meeting wourd be rather a long time to delay every piece of work. This might do under ordinary circumstances, but the association thought tnere knight be special ce.ses requiring almost immediate attention; but no doubt the Board would not strictly adhere to the letter of the matter, should it be proved that the urgency of such cases needed special attention. Mr. SHAW said that if the new bye-laws, were worth any- thing at all, they ought to be applied to every case, and it could not reasonably be supposed that the carrying of them out would prove any greater hardship to the Bridgewater of Ellesmere trustees than to builders or any other persons who tad land in Runcorn. Mr. P. SPEAKMAN considered that the bye-laws ought to have been laid upon the table for several weeks, as the pass- ing of them was quite a new departure. He was certainly in favour of them being referred back to the Highway and Sanitary Committee for reconsideration. Mr. HANDLEY protested against the observations made by Mr. Speakman, on the ground that they reflected very seriously upon the Bye-Laws Committee, and he, as chair- man of that committee, did not feel inclined to sit down quietly under such an unfounded accusation. A great amount of time and patience had been spent in preparing the new bye-laws, and at the time that work was being carried out, the action which the committee was taking was perfectly well known to every commissioner and the master builders. Indeed before the byelaws were finally approved, the master builders forwarded an objection to them; and the order for the insertion of advertisements being inserted in the newspapers notifying the proposed alterations, and giv- ing particulars as Eo when and where they could be inspected, was given at a well attended Board meeting, held some two or three months ago. In order to make it doubly certain that every ratepayer should know about the matter, a copy of the amended bye-laws was placed out- side the doors of the Commissioners' offices. The bye-laws could thus be seen without a single penny being expended upon the purchase of them. He had also spoken to several builders in the town upon the matter, and they had told him, about ten days ago, that they had no objection to the bye-laws, but that, in fact, they considered them a great improvement upon the old ones. Dr. McDouciam, had a strong objection to Mr. Feredly Smith making suggestions to the Board. If they entered upon this matter at that meeting it would open a very wide field for discussion ; and he would. therefore, move that it be considered at the meeting on Friday night. Mr. HAZLEHURST seconded the proposition. The CLERK: I think that we ought to acknowledge the letter. Mr. HANDLEY : Yes, acknowledge Mr. Smith's cummuni- cation in the ordinary way. Mr. MEADOWCROFT : I would say acknowledge it, and state that it will receive the consideration of the Board. It was agreed that the suggestion of Mr. Meadowcroft should be adopted, and the subject dropped. HIGHWAY COMMITTEE.—IMPORTANT TO BUILDERS.

Mr. NORMAN moved, and Mr. WILLIAMS seconded, the motion for the adoption of the minutes of the Highway and Sanitary Committee, which contained the following items of interest :—The correspondence and report of the Medical Officer with reference to Mr. Lello's application for permis- sion to turn tannery sewerage into the main sewer in Halton-road had been considered, and it had been resolved that the gentlemen referred to should be asked to state in writing the particulars of the ingredients of the sevSage, and that his reply should be submitted to the Medical Officer for his observations. ItesolvAi that the Surveyor see the manager of the Glycerine Works with reference to the emission of smoke and the drainage of the manufactory. A letter had been received from Mr. H. White stating that he was enlarging Trinity schools, and claiming exemption from depositing plans. The committee had instructed the Sur- veyor to inhibit Mr. White from proceeding with the works until plans wet% submitted. The Inspector of Nuisances having complained of his suit of uniform having become so shabby that he was unable to appear in it, it was recom- mended that he be provided with a new one. The Surveyor having reported that wooden sheds had been erected on property in Sewell, Vine, and Egerton-streets, a resolution had been passed that notices be served on the occupiers to remove them. A sub-committee, consisting of Messrs. A special meeting was held on the list ult. to consider the fouling of the fountain water. The Surveyor and Medical Officer were instructed to make a thorough in- vestigation as to the cause of the pollution and repot t upon it. At a meeting on the 3rd inst., a letter was read from Mr. Lello, and the report of the Medical Officer as to the ingredients in the sewage from the proposed new taanery iii Halton-road. It was recommended that Mr. Leila be allowed to drain into the sewer in Halton-road on paying is. per annum, and giving an undertaking to discontinue the use'of the sewer on receiving two weeks notice, and also agreeing to pay the cost of repairing any damage, and of removing any nuisance or inconvenience caused thereby. The Secre- tary was instructed to supply the Local Government Board with information as to the works within the Commissioners' district which would be effected by the Alkali Works Regu- lation Act, 1881. •Recommended that the seal of the Board be affixed to the proposed building bye-laws, and that they be forwarded to the Local Government Board for confirma- tion. The Secretary was requested to submit to the next meeting of the committee information as to the arrangement between the Commissioners and the Bridgewater Trustees as to the services of the Surveyor in connection with the con- struction of certain street in Duke's Field. The Law Clerk was instructed to take steps to forward the erection of the Bridge slope. MERSEY MISSIONS TO SEAMEN (RUNCORN BRANCH.)—It has been decided to build or purchase a House for the Missionary connected with the above branch, Donations in aid of the same will be thankfully received by the Treasurer, E. A. Chorlton, Esq. Parr's Banking Company, Runcorn. It has also been decided to hold a CHRISTMAS TREE andSALE OF WORK on Tz.unsDAY and FRIDAY. DECEMBER 29th and 30th, 1881, in the PUBLIC HALL RUNCORN. The foPow- ing ladies have kindly consented to preside at the stalls and to receive all parcels or donations towards the same ;—Mrs. Lloyd Wigg, Mrs. Dr. Steele, Miss Barclay. Miss Williams, Percival's- lane ; Miss Mouritz, High-street; Miss Norman, Greenway- road ; Miss Garrett, Albert-street; Miss S. E. Sts i ham, Trenth- am-street; Misses Owen, Brackley-street ; Miss Coleburn, Church-street ; Miss Davies. Brackley-street ; Mrs. E Bellin- ley, Astridge-street ; Mrs. Croley, Bridge-street; Mrs. Banke.s, Weston ; Miss Clarke,.Weaver Villa, Weston Point; Mr. Shaw, Missionary; or any of the Sunday School Teachers. Weekly Sewing Meetings will be held at the Mission-room, Bottom Locks, every Wednesday from 2to 9 p.m. Tea will be pro- vided at 6 o'clock. Workers, 6d. each; visitors, Is. All interested in the work will have la hearty welcome.

WARRINGTON GRAMMAR SCHOOL. FREE SCHOLARSHIPS. An EXAMINATION, to elect four free scholars, will be held at the GRAMMAR SCHOOL, at 10 a.m., on FRIDAY, DEC. Nth, 1881. CansUclates must be under 12 years of age on September 30th, 1881. These scholarship are open only to boys who have been for three years under instruction at some public elemen- tary school within the school district of Warrington. All applications for admission to the Examination must be sent in before Thursday, December Ist; and must be accom- panied with certificates of age, of character, and of three years' attendance at a public elementary school. For further par- Denies apply to the HEAD MASTER.

RE JOHN BLINSTON, Deceased.—Pursuant to the Statute 22 and 23 Victoria. cap. 35, intituled "An Act to further amend the law of property and to relieve trustees," NOTICE is Ilmav GIVEN, that all CREDITORS and other persons having any CLAIMS or DEMANDS upon or against the estate of JOHN I3E.INSTON, late of Statham-within-Lymm, in the county of Chester, gentleman, and recently residing at Altrincham, in the said county, who died on or about the Fourteenth aay of October. one thow,and eight hundred and eighty-one, and letters of administration of whose personal estate and effects were granted by the District Registry at Chester, of the Probate Division of Her Majesty's High Court of Justice, on the First day of November. one thou,and eight hundred and eighty-one, to William Rlinston, of Statham, aforesaid, farmer, are HEREBY REQUIRED IO SEND in the particulars of their cr..A.This and DEMANDS in writing, to us theundersigned on or before the Twenty-Fifth day of Decem ber next, after which date the Administrator will proceed to distribute the assets of the said deceased amongst the parties entitled thereto, having regard only to the claims or demands of which the said Administrator shall then have had notice. And NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN, that the said Administrator will not be liable for the assets or any part thereof, so distributed, to any person of whose debt, claim, or demand, he shall not then have had notice.—Dated this Third day of November, 1881. RIDGWAY & WORSLEY, 2, Cairo-street, Warrington, Solicitors for the said Administrator,

IN PARLIAMENT—SESSION 1882. QAIN T. HELENS (CORPORATION) WATER. (Construction of Waterworks—Compulsory Purchase of Land—Extension of Water Limits—Levy and Alteration of Rates and Charges—Borrowing of Money—Ameltd- ment, Repeal, and Incorporation of Acts). NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN, that Application is intended to be made to Parliament in the ensuing Session by the Mayor, Aldermen, and Burgesses of the town of Skint Helens, in the County of Lancaster (hereinafter called the Corporation), for leave to bring in a Bill for all or some of the following purposes (that is to say) To empower the Corporation to make and maintain the works hsreinafter described, or some of them, that is to say- 1. The Kirkby Pumping Station.—A shaft or well (to be sunk to an uncertain depth) with pumps, engines, and appliances connected therewith, wholly situate in the • township of Kirkby, in the parish of Walton-on-the. Hill, in and near the southeast corner of a field, which adjoins, on the south side thereof, Old Rough Cattage, stack yard, and croft, which lie and abut on the northerly side of Old Rough-lane, and which field iselongs, or is reputed to belong, to the Earl of Sefton, and is in the occupation of Thomas Owen. 2. An Aqueduct or Line of Pipes, commencing in the said township and parish, at tho said intended shaft or well, and terminating in the township of Knowsley, in the parish of Huyton, by a junction with the aque- duct hereinafter described in Moss-lane, at a point fourteen chains or thereabouts south of the junction of Scarisbrick-brow with Old Molly's-lane, which aque- duct will be wholly situate in the townships of Kirkby and Knowsley, and parishes of Walton-on-the-Hill and Hutton. 3. The Knowsley Pumping Station —A shaft or well (to be sunk to an uncertain depth) with pumps, engines, and appliances connected therewith, wholly situate in the township of Knowsley, in the parish of Huyton, in the north-easterly portion of a field abutting on the north-, west on the brook which forms the boundary of the townships of Kirkby and Knowsley, and abutting as to part of such field, and on the easterly side thereof on Moss-lane, and on the north-easterly side thereof ' on the garden belonging, or attached to a house o: cottage in Moss-lane, in the occupation of one Thomas Ratcliffe, and which field belongs, or is reputed to belong, to the Earl of Derby, and is in the occupation of Joseph Hewitt. 4. An Aqueduct or Line of Pipes, commencing in the said township of Knowsley and parish of Huyton, at the last-mentioned intended shaft or well, anal terminating In the townshipof Eccleston, In the parish of Prescot, in Holt-lane, at its junction with Scholes-lane, and by a junction with the existing aqueduct of the Corpora- tion, which intended aqueduct will be wholly situate in the townships of Knowsley and Eccleston, and parishes of Huyton and Prescot. All which intended works will be wholly situate in the County of Lancaster. Together with all proper and necessary wells, shafts, tun- nels, drifts, adits, pipes, valves, syphons, hydrants, junctions, tanks, basins, engines, pumps, buildings, embankments roads, and other works connected with the shafts or wells, aqueducts and works aforesaid, and which may be necessary or proper for taking, pumping, impounding, using, and distributing the waters intended to be taken. To empower the Corporation for the purposes of the intended works and Act, to purchase or acquire by compulsion or agree- ment, or to take on lease, any lands, houses, or buildings, or to appropriate any lands, houses, or buildings belonging to them In the townships, parishes, and county aforesaid, and any rights, or easements in, over, or connected with any lands, houses, or buildings in the townships, parishes, and county aforesaid, and on the sale of lands to reserve water and other rights. To empower the Corporation to take, pump, divert, impound, appropriate, and use for the purposes of their water under- taking, or other the purposes of the intended Act, all springs, streams, and waters which may be found in, upon, or under any lands acquired or held by the Corporation under the powers of the intended Act, or which can, or may be taken, or intercepted by the intended works or some of them. To empower the Corporation to deviate in the construction of the intended works laterally and vertically to the extent to be shown on the plans and sections to be deposited as herein- after mentioned or to be defined in the intended Act:

and renew mains, //ewer.. and In, through, a long, under, across,•and over any public highways, streets, roads, streams, paths, tramways and railways, and for the purposes of the intended Act to break up, cross, alter, divert, stop up (either temporarily or permanently), and inter- fere with roads, streets, highways, courts, alleys, footpaths, bridges, tramways, railways, sewers, drains, streams, brooks, water-courses, mains,,pipes. and telegraphs within Vie parishes, townships, and places aforesaid. To extend the limits of the Corporation for supplying water to all places within the said townships of Kirkby and Knowsley. To empower the Corporation for all or any of the purposes of the intended Act to demand, recover, and levy rates, rents, and charges for and in respect of the supply of water, to in- crease or vary existing rates, rents, and charges, and confer ex- emptions therefrom, and to apply any money belonging to, or under the control of the Corporation to all or any of the objects and purposes of the intended Act, and to borrow money for the purposes of the intended Act, and to mortgage or charge the rates, rents, tolls, or charges levied or leviable by them, and their Gas and Water undertakings, lands and nroperty, or some of them, as security therefor, with power to issue debentures, debenture stock, and annuity certificates, charge- able upon the securities in afvresaid, or any of them, and to make provision for the repayment of money to be so borrowed. To vary or extinguish all existing rights and privileges, which would or might ia any way prevent or Interfere with or delay the accimplishment of any of the objects of the intended Act, and to confer other rights and privileges. To repeal or amend all or some of the provisions of the follow- ing Local Act, and pub lc Acts of a local character, namely: The St. Heless Improvement Act, 1869. The Local Govern- ment Board's Provisional Orders Confirmation (Belper Union, etc.) Act. 1817. The Local Government Board's Provisional Orders Confirmation (Abingdon, etc.) Act, 1878. The Local Government Board's (Provisional Orders Confirmation (Aber- gavenny Union, eta ) Act, 1879, and all other Acts relating to the Corporation. The Liverpool Corporation Waterworks Act, 1847. The Liverpool Corporation Waterworks Act, 1850, and all Acts relating to the Waterworks undertaking of the Mayor, Aldermen, and Citizens of the City of Liverpool. To incorporate with or without alterations and amendments all or some of the provisions of the following Public Acts, namely: The Commissioners' Clauses Act, 1847. The Lands Clauses Consolidation Acts, 1815. 1860, and 1869. The Water- works' Clauses Acts, 1547 and 1863. The Local Loans Act, 1875, and the Provisions of the Railways' Clauses Consolidation Act, 1845, with respect to the temporary occupation of lands and all Acts amending the same respectively or any of them, and all or some of the Provisions or the St. Helens Improvement Act, 1869. On or before the 30th day of November instant, duplicate , plans, and sections, and books of reference to such plans, to- I gether with a copy of this notice as published in the London Gazette, will be deposited for public inspection with the Clerk of the Peace for the County of Lancaster, at his office at Preston, and on or before the same day a copy of so much of the said plans, sections. and books of reference as relates to the several parishes in or through which the said intended works are pro- posed to be made, together with a copy of this notice, will on or before the said 30th day of November be deposited with the Clerk of each such parishat his residence. Printed copies of the intended Act or Bill, will, on or before the 21st day of December next, be deposited in the Private Bill Offiee of the House of Commons. Dated this Fourth day of November. 1881. THOILAS BREWIS, • Town Clerk, St. Helens. SHARPE, PARKERS, PRITCHARD, & SHARPE. q, Bridge-street, Westrninister, Parliamentary Agents.

Widnes, on and after Tuesday, the Ist day of November, 1881. Copies of the specification, bill of quantities, schedule of prices, and form of tender may be obtained, on payment of three guineas in each case, to the undersigned, which will be returned on receipt of a bond fide tender, accom- panied by the bill of quantities, schedule of prices, specifica- tion, and the receipt given for the three guineas deposited. Sealed tenders endorsed " Tender for Construction of New Main Sewer, contract No. must be addressed to the Chair- man of the Joint High Way and 'Health Committee, and dei'vered at the office of the undersigned not later than 12 o'clock on Thursday, the Ist day of December, 1881. Tenders will not he accepted unless made out on the form above- named, with all the items in the bill of quantities and schedule of prices, fully priced and moneyed out.
